rows.stem: The region of chromatin that are actively transcribed are thought to be :
rows.solution: Chromatin is packed to different degrees in the nucleus. The region that is **loosely packed** and stains light is **euchromatin**; the region that is densely packed and stains dark is heterochromatin. Euchromatin is said to be **transcriptionally active**, while heterochromatin is inactive. So the answer is option (B) Euchromatin.

rows.stem:
Given below are few statements with reference to the ovaries of the human female reproductive system :
(i) It is 2 – 4 cm in length and is connected to the pelvic wall by tendons.
(ii) It is covered by a thin epithelium which encloses the ovarian stroma.
(iii) The stroma is divided into a peripheral medulla and an inner cortex.
(iv) The ovaries are the primary female sex organs that produce the female gamete (ovum).
(v) Ovaries are located one on each side of the lower abdomen.
Choose the option with all true statements from the given options :
rows.solution:
- (i) False: each ovary is about 2 to 4 cm in length, but it is connected to the pelvic wall and the uterus by **ligaments**, not tendons.
- (ii) True: each ovary is covered by a **thin epithelium** which encloses the ovarian stroma.
- (iii) False: the stroma is divided into a **peripheral cortex** and an **inner medulla**; the statement has them the wrong way round.
- (iv) True: the ovaries are the **primary female sex organs** that produce the female gamete (ovum) and several steroid hormones.
- (v) True: the ovaries are located one on each side of the **lower abdomen**.

So the true statements are (ii), (iv) and (v). So the answer is option (C) (ii), (iv) and (v).

rows.stem: The approach of sequencing the whole set of genome, including all the coding and non-coding sequences in HGP is :
rows.solution:
The Human Genome Project followed two major approaches.
- **Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs)**: identifying all the genes that are expressed as RNA.
- **Sequence Annotation**: the blind approach of simply **sequencing the whole set of genome**, containing all the **coding and non-coding sequences**, and later assigning different regions in the sequence with functions.

So the answer is option (C) Sequence Annotation.

rows.stem: In the pedigree chart given below, what should be the genotype of the indicated member ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED: a three-generation pedigree. Generation I is a mated couple (square and circle); generation II is their six children (four sons, two daughters), one daughter married to an outside male; generation III is that couple's three children (one son, two daughters). The '?' sits under the other daughter of generation II. Which symbols are shaded (affected) decides the genotype, so the shading is withheld here. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
Reading the pedigree:
- The couple in generation I are both unaffected, yet two of their children (a son and the indicated daughter) are affected. A trait that appears in children of unaffected parents is **recessive**, and both parents must be carriers.
- The indicated member is an **affected daughter of an unaffected father**. An X-linked recessive trait cannot do this (the father would have to carry the allele on his single X and so be affected), so the trait is **autosomal recessive**.
- In generation III, the unaffected couple again has an affected son, which fits the same pattern.

An individual who shows an autosomal recessive trait must be homozygous recessive. So the answer is option (D) aa.

rows.stem: The lobed organ located near the heart and beneath the breast bone in humans is :
rows.solution: The **thymus** is a **lobed organ** located near the heart and beneath the breastbone. It is a primary lymphoid organ: immature lymphocytes mature into antigen-sensitive T-lymphocytes here. The thymus is quite large at the time of birth and keeps reducing in size with age, so that by puberty it is very small. So the answer is option (C) Thymus.

rows.stem: Unisexuality of flowers prevents which process ?
rows.solution:
When a plant bears only unisexual flowers, no flower has both anthers and stigma, so pollen cannot reach the stigma of the **same flower**: **autogamy is prevented**.
- In a **monoecious** plant such as castor or maize, male and female flowers are on the same plant, so pollen can still pass to another flower of the same plant: **geitonogamy is not prevented**.
- Only the **dioecious** condition (male and female flowers on different plants, as in papaya) prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy.

Unisexuality as such therefore prevents autogamy, but not geitonogamy. So the answer is option (D) Autogamy, but not Geitonogamy.

rows.stem: Which of the following combinations is a correct example of convergent evolution in Placental mammals and Australian marsupials ?

options.label: A
options.text: Placental Mammals: Anteater, Australian Marsupials: Lemur

options.label: B
options.text: Placental Mammals: Numbat, Australian Marsupials: Bobcat

options.label: C
options.text: Placental Mammals: Tasmanian tiger cat, Australian Marsupials: Anteater

options.label: D
options.text: Placental Mammals: Lemur, Australian Marsupials: Spotted cuscus

rows.solution:
In convergent evolution, Australian marsupials and placental mammals that live in similar habitats have come to look alike although they evolved independently. The recognised pairs (placental mammal and its marsupial counterpart) include anteater and **numbat**, lemur and **spotted cuscus**, bobcat and **Tasmanian tiger cat**, and mole and marsupial mole.
- The first pairing lists the lemur, a placental mammal, under marsupials.
- The second lists the numbat (a marsupial) under placental mammals and the bobcat (a placental mammal) under marsupials.
- The third puts the Tasmanian tiger cat under placental mammals and the anteater under marsupials, both the wrong way round.

The lemur (placental mammal) and the spotted cuscus (Australian marsupial) are a correct pair. So the answer is option (D) Placental Mammals: Lemur, Australian Marsupials: Spotted cuscus.

rows.subtopic: Isolation, Cutting and Amplification of DNA
rows.stem: Isolation of DNA from a bacterial cell can be achieved by using :
rows.solution: To isolate DNA, the cell must first be broken open by treating it with enzymes that digest its wall. The enzyme depends on what the wall is made of: **lysozyme for bacteria**, cellulase for plant cells and chitinase for fungi. RNA is then removed with ribonuclease and proteins with protease, but neither of these opens the bacterial cell. So the answer is option (B) Lysozyme.

rows.stem:
Match the terms in Column-I with their description in Column-II and choose the correct option.
| Column-I (Terms) | Column-II (Descriptions) |
|---|---|
| a. Dominance | (i) Many genes govern a single character. |
| b. Codominance | (ii) In a heterozygote organism, only one allele expresses itself. |
| c. Pleiotropy | (iii) In a heterozygous organism, both alleles express themselves fully. |
| d. Polygenic inheritance | (iv) A single gene influences many characters. |
rows.solution:
- **Dominance**: in a heterozygote, only one allele expresses itself, so a matches (ii).
- **Codominance**: in a heterozygote, both alleles express themselves fully, as in the AB blood group, so b matches (iii).
- **Pleiotropy**: a single gene influences many characters (phenotypic expressions), as in phenylketonuria, so c matches (iv).
- **Polygenic inheritance**: many genes govern a single character, as in human skin colour, so d matches (i).

So the answer is option (A) a-(ii), b-(iii), c-(iv), d-(i).

rows.stem:
Which enzyme(s) will be produced in a bacterial cell in which 'UAG' is inserted in the 'lac-y gene' due to mutation ?
Choose the correct option :
rows.solution:
The lac operon has three structural genes, z, y and a, transcribed together as one **polycistronic mRNA** and translated in that order.
- The z gene codes for \(\beta\)-galactosidase, the y gene for permease and the a gene for transacetylase.
- UAG is a **stop codon**. Inserted into the y gene by mutation, it is a premature stop (a nonsense mutation).
- The z gene lies before the mutation, so it is translated completely and \(\beta\)-galactosidase is produced.
- Translation ends inside the y gene, so a complete permease is not made, and the a gene lying after it is not translated either (the polar effect of the nonsense mutation), so transacetylase is not produced.

Only \(\beta\)-galactosidase is produced. So the answer is option (C) \(\beta\)-galactosidase.

rows.stem: Large scale industrial production of citric acid for human welfare is done using the microbe :
rows.solution: Microbes are used in industry to produce organic acids: **Aspergillus niger** (a fungus) produces **citric acid**, Acetobacter aceti acetic acid, Clostridium butylicum butyric acid and Lactobacillus lactic acid. Streptococcus produces streptokinase, and Trichoderma is a biocontrol agent and the source of cyclosporin A. So the answer is option (B) Aspergillus sp.

rows.stem: In a DNA, percentage of thymine is 20. What is the percentage of Guanine ?
rows.solution:
By Chargaff's rule, in double-stranded DNA the amount of adenine equals thymine and the amount of guanine equals cytosine.
- Thymine = 20%, so adenine = 20%, and A + T = 40%.
- G + C = 100% \(-\) 40% = 60%.
- Guanine = cytosine, so guanine = 60% \(\div\) 2 = 30%.

So the answer is option (B) 30%.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Lymphocytes arise from bone marrow and present in the blood and lymph and serve as natural killer cells.
Reason (R) : Lymphocytes migrate to thymus, where they develop into T-cells and begin to mature.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution: The Assertion is true: lymphocytes, like all blood cells, arise from stem cells in the **bone marrow**, a primary lymphoid organ, and they are present in the **blood and lymph**. Natural killer (NK) cells are a type of lymphocyte that kill virus-infected and tumour cells as part of cellular barriers of innate immunity. The Reason is also true: immature lymphocytes **migrate to the thymus**, where they develop into antigen-sensitive **T-lymphocytes**. The marking scheme treats the Reason as explaining the Assertion, although strictly the Reason describes how T-cells mature rather than why lymphocytes serve as natural killer cells. So both statements are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem: Name a blood related autosomal Mendelian disorder. Why is it called as Mendelian disorder ? How is the disorder transmitted from parents to offspring ?
rows.solution:
**Sickle-cell anaemia** (or thalassemia) is a blood-related autosomal Mendelian disorder.

Why it is called a Mendelian disorder:
- It is determined by an **alteration or mutation in a single gene**. In sickle-cell anaemia, a single base substitution in the gene for the \(\beta\)-globin chain of haemoglobin replaces glutamic acid (Glu) by valine (Val) at the sixth position.
- It is transmitted to the offspring on the **same lines as Mendel studied in the garden pea**, so its pattern of inheritance can be traced in a family by **pedigree analysis**.

How it is transmitted: it is an **autosomal recessive** trait. The disease appears only in the homozygous condition, \(\text{Hb}^{\text{S}}\text{Hb}^{\text{S}}\); heterozygous individuals, \(\text{Hb}^{\text{A}}\text{Hb}^{\text{S}}\), appear unaffected but are **carriers**. It passes from parents to offspring when **both partners are carriers** (heterozygous):
- Parents: \(\text{Hb}^{\text{A}}\text{Hb}^{\text{S}}\) \(\times\) \(\text{Hb}^{\text{A}}\text{Hb}^{\text{S}}\).
- Gametes: \(\text{Hb}^{\text{A}}\) and \(\text{Hb}^{\text{S}}\) from each parent.
- Offspring: \(\text{Hb}^{\text{A}}\text{Hb}^{\text{A}}\) (normal), \(\text{Hb}^{\text{A}}\text{Hb}^{\text{S}}\) (carrier) and \(\text{Hb}^{\text{S}}\text{Hb}^{\text{S}}\) (diseased) in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1.

So there is a 25 per cent chance that a child of two carriers suffers from the disease.

rows.stem:
(i) Explain why the insecticidal protein producing by Bacillus thuringiensis does not kill the bacteria itself.
(ii) How has man exploited this protein to produce cotton bollworm resistant Bt cotton plant ?
rows.solution:
(i) **Bacillus thuringiensis** produces protein crystals during a particular phase of its growth. These crystals contain a toxic insecticidal protein, but inside the bacterium the **Bt toxin exists as an inactive protoxin**, so it does not kill the bacterium. The protoxin becomes active only in the **alkaline pH of the insect gut**, which solubilises the crystals. The activated toxin binds to the surface of the midgut epithelial cells and creates pores, causing the cells to swell and lyse, and the insect dies. The alkaline pH needed for activation is not available in the bacterium itself.

(ii) The Bt toxin is coded by genes named **cry**. The proteins encoded by the genes **cryIAc and cryIIAb control the cotton bollworms**. These specific Bt toxin genes were isolated from Bacillus thuringiensis and **incorporated into cotton plants** using recombinant DNA technology. The transgenic Bt cotton plants make the toxin themselves, so a bollworm feeding on the plant takes in the protein, which is activated in its alkaline gut and kills it. This makes the crop resistant to the pest and reduces the use of chemical insecticides.

rows.stem:
(i) Identify the selectable markers labelled as 'a' and 'b' in the given diagram of E. coli vector.
(ii) How is coding sequence of enzyme \(\beta\)-galactosidase considered a better marker than the ones identified by you in the diagram ? Explain.
(iii) List any two uses of cloning vector in biotechnology.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED: the E. coli cloning vector pBR322 drawn as a ring, with the restriction sites Cla I, Pvu I, Pst I, BamH I, Sal I and Pvu II marked around it, and ori and rop labelled inside the ring. Two further segments of the ring are labelled 'a' and 'b'; which genes those segments are is what part (i) asks, so their positions relative to the sites are withheld here. Page idx 24.
rows.solution:
(i) In the E. coli cloning vector pBR322, 'a' is \(\text{amp}^{\text{R}}\), the **ampicillin resistance gene**, and 'b' is \(\text{tet}^{\text{R}}\), the **tetracycline resistance gene**. These are the vector's two selectable markers.

(ii) The coding sequence of \(\beta\)-galactosidase is a better marker because of **insertional inactivation**:
- The recombinant DNA is inserted within the coding sequence of the enzyme \(\beta\)-galactosidase, which inactivates the enzyme.
- When the bacteria are grown on a medium containing a **chromogenic substrate**, colonies whose plasmid has no insert produce **blue colour**, while recombinant colonies, with the enzyme inactivated, produce **no colour**. So recombinants are told apart from non-recombinants by colour on a single plate.
- Selection by inactivation of an antibiotic resistance gene is **cumbersome**, because it needs simultaneous plating on **two plates having different antibiotics** (for example, recombinants grow on ampicillin but not on tetracycline when the insert sits in the tetracycline resistance gene).

(iii) Two uses of cloning vectors in biotechnology:
- They are used to make **multiple copies of the desired DNA** (gene of interest), since the vector replicates within the host along with the linked DNA.
- They are used to **transfer the gene of interest into the host cell**, where it can be expressed and its product obtained.
